clue.text: Hat girl booked

definitions.meaning: a soft felt hat with a narrow brim and dented crown
a girl in a book: the heroine of George du Maurier's 1894 novel, who gave the hat its name

explanation.definitionFit: The felt hat took its name from the stage version of du Maurier's novel, whose title heroine wore one.

clue.text: The black-hearted thirteen chopped this tree

indicators.note: black-hearted means the black letter is set at the heart of the other word
chopped up means the letters of the word thirteen are cut about and rearranged

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A grim tale of thirteen wicked men felling a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black-hearted' reads as 'with black at its heart', and 'chopped' as cut up and rearranged, though the surface suggests a grim gang felling timber.
explanation.definitionFit: The terebinth is a Mediterranean tree of the pistachio family, source of turpentine.

clue.text: One spirit includes that classic single element

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: includes means the spirit's letters take the following pieces inside them

parts.note: rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane
id is Latin, a classical language, for 'that'
single, one, gives the numeral I

explanation.surface: A single classic spirit, mentioned as a fine drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classic' points to Latin, where ID means 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Iridium is a hard, dense metallic chemical element of the platinum group.

clue.text: Drivers should avoid it — and what passes through it

definitions.meaning: a narrow stretch of road where traffic jams build
the narrow neck of a glass vessel, which liquid pours through

explanation.definitionFit: A road narrowing is named after the slim upper part of a bottle, through which contents pour.

clue.text: Aircraft spotter out every Sunday

definitions.meaning: a person watching the skies for planes, as in wartime defence
a British Sunday newspaper published each week

explanation.definitionFit: A watcher of planes is a spotter; the British Sunday paper of the same name appears weekly.

clue.text: Build-up for The Ring

parts.note: a structure built up high so that its chimes can be rung, not a prelude to Wagner's opera cycle

explanation.definitionFit: A tall structure housing bells is built so that they can be rung.

clue.text: Book Horatio loved

definitions.meaning: Lady Hamilton, the mistress of Admiral Horatio Nelson

explanation.definitionFit: Austen's novel is named for its heroine, and Nelson's lover Lady Hamilton bore the same first name.

clue.text: The gloss seems to disappear about mid-April

indicators.note: about means the first word's letters go around the next piece

parts.note: to vanish is to pass from sight, seeming to disappear

indicators.note: mid- picks the middle letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A shiny finish fading away in the spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-April' gives R, the middle letter of APRIL, and 'about' puts VANISH around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnish is a clear coating that gives wood a glossy finish.

clue.text: Sail with two boys

parts.note: Roy is a boy's name
Al is a boy's name, short for Alan or Albert

explanation.surface: A pair of lads go out sailing together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two boys' gives two short names side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: On a square-rigged ship, the royal is a small sail set above the topgallant.

clue.text: Bit of a blow, say ? So enfold in a shawl

indicators.note: say means the following word is spoken, giving the sound of another spelling

parts.note: a rap is a sharp knock, a small blow

explanation.surface: A gust of wind prompts someone to bundle up in a shawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap is to wind a covering around, as a shawl round the shoulders.

clue.text: One enlisted to make noisy whoopee

annotationWithheld.why: One enlisted to make noisy whoopee: I inside ROSTER, where 'enlisted' (en-list-ed, in a list) is both the container indicator and the source of ROSTER, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: One enlisted to make noisy whoopee

clue.text: Swimmer beat victim

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
prey is a hunted creature, a victim

explanation.surface: A swimmer thrashes a hapless victim.
explanation.definitionFit: The lamprey is an eel-like jawless fish that swims and feeds by attaching to other fish.

clue.text: Route taken by a horsewoman — about to change her name, say ?

definitions.text: Route taken by a horsewoman — about to change her name, say ?

parts.words: Route taken by a horsewoman — about to change her name, say ?
parts.note: a track for riders, whose first word sounds like the adjective for a bride, a woman about to take a new surname

explanation.definitionFit: A track for riders and horses, sounding like a bride's way to the altar.

clue.text: Dramatist said to have a way with him

definitions.meaning: the familiar first name of Shakespeare

definitions.text: said to have a way with him
definitions.meaning: the proverb says where there is resolve there is a way

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's first name; the proverb pairs determination with finding a way.

clue.text: It comes handy to one helping at board meetings

definitions.text: It comes handy to one helping at board meetings

parts.words: It comes handy to one helping at board meetings
parts.note: a serving utensil used by someone dishing out food at the dinner table, not at a company board

explanation.definitionFit: A large serving utensil is used to dish out portions at the dining table.

clue.text: So-called lion man perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the words lion man could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone is dubbed the lion man, though it may be a nickname only.
explanation.definitionFit: Nominal means existing in name only, so called but not really so.

clue.text: Men of action

parts.note: people who bring legal actions in court, not daring adventurers

explanation.definitionFit: Parties to a lawsuit bring or defend legal actions.

clue.text: Come safely through the elements

definitions.meaning: to survive a crisis or storm
wind, rain and sun, the atmospheric conditions

explanation.definitionFit: To ride out a storm is to survive it; the elements are the atmospheric conditions.

clue.text: Like the day of the Zinoviev scandal?

definitions.text: Like the day of the Zinoviev scandal?

parts.words: Like the day of the Zinoviev scandal?
parts.note: a memorable day is described with the same phrase

explanation.walkthrough: The Zinoviev letter of 1924 was a forged Soviet message that damaged Britain's Labour Party before an election.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorable day is called a red-letter day, after saints' days printed in red; Zinoviev's was a Red letter.

clue.text: Quarrelsome companion for Cerberus?

parts.note: a spiteful, fiery woman, pictured as an infernal feline beside the underworld's guard dog

explanation.definitionFit: A hellcat is a spiteful, violent woman; Cerberus is the hound of the underworld.

clue.text: Book of words needed for the Roman Law I study

parts.note: lex is the Latin word for law
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A dictionary required by a student of Roman law.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a dictionary, a reference work listing words.

clue.text: Right happy when told

parts.note: elated means delighted, happy

explanation.surface: Someone is quite pleased on hearing the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Related can mean narrated or recounted, a story told.

clue.text: Trifling goes against one in judicial proceedings

indicators.note: in means the following pieces sit inside the court case word

parts.note: a trial is a hearing in court
V, for versus, means against, as in case names
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A petty matter goes to court against someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes' is only a link; V for versus is the legal shorthand in case names such as Smith v Jones.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial means of little importance, trifling.

clue.text: Not extraordinary to find herein inspiration for a sermon

indicators.note: herein says the letters are found inside the words Not extraordinary

explanation.surface: An ordinary passage turns out to inspire a preacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher's sermon takes a Bible passage, its text, as its starting point.

clue.text: To select detail in a subject

indicators.note: de-tail means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to pick is to select

explanation.surface: Choosing fine points within a theme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detail' is read as de-tail: PICK loses its final K.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the theme or matter discussed, a subject.

clue.text: Like savage tigers disturbed at this

definitions.text: Like savage tigers disturbed at this

indicators.note: disturbed means the letters of savage tigers are rearranged, and they equal the answer plus those of at

explanation.surface: Wild tigers, when disturbed, turn hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite: the letters of SAVAGE TIGERS rearranged make the answer and AT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Savage, disturbed tigers are ready to attack, hostile in manner.

clue.text: Flier could thus lay low an ace

definitions.meaning: a sandpiper of Europe, the male with a frilled collar

definitions.text: could thus lay low an ace
definitions.meaning: in card games, trumping a card, even an ace

explanation.definitionFit: The ruff is a wading bird; at bridge or whist, to trump a card beats even an ace.

clue.text: Ancient Mariner's story upset this Muslim VIP

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Coleridge's poem is The Rime of the Ancient Mariner

explanation.surface: Coleridge's poem offends a Muslim dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir is a Muslim ruler or commander, a dignitary.

clue.text: R U Forward, pedlar

definitions.meaning: in Rugby Union, a forward plays in the scrum, the pack
a travelling seller who carries goods in a bundle on the back

explanation.walkthrough: R U is Rugby Union, whose forwards are collectively the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar carries a bundle of wares on his back; a rugby forward plays in the scrum.

clue.text: He sells proverbially comfortable bedding

parts.note: an ease is proverbially a bed of roses, so this trader sells blooms for flower beds

explanation.definitionFit: A flower seller trades in roses, the stuff of the proverbial comfortable bed.

clue.text: Do artists entering race provide difference in tone ?

parts.note: to do someone is to con or swindle them

indicators.note: entering means the artists go inside the race

parts.note: the TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist; RAS the plural

explanation.surface: Artists joining a race give a contrast of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is a verb meaning swindle, not a party; the TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race, and RA a Royal Academician.
explanation.definitionFit: In art, a striking difference in shade or colour is a contrast.

clue.text: He finds a corner by the river

definitions.text: He finds a corner by the river

parts.note: an angle is a corner

explanation.surface: A fisherman settles in a nook on the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisherman sits by the riverbank, finding his angle on the water.
